claim: A key reads as the place's purpose when it is seen, lit, from a vantage before it can be reached: in Gravesend the machine hall's key is seen over a rail from a deck, lit under its own hood, with the lever that makes it safe the second thing seen; the arcade's key is in sight from the street door across a fallen gallery. E3M6 shows its moon key so, up between two drums.
evidence: E3M6 sprite 355 (kItemKeyMoon) stands in s410, a floor 32,768 above s413 beside the higher s378 and s379 (record checked 2026-11-26; the drums are as Gravesend's notes describe it, not re-seen in a frame)
use: Put a key's light on it and a first view of it from where the player enters; make the way to it indirect.
